findings.claim: The closing divine title is called the middle member of a byte-tier title pair without any tier disclosed for the token itself, which returns tier NONE against both legs of that pair.
findings.grounds: device_notes writes that אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ (oshb:Isa.40.8) 'stands as the middle member of a byte-tier title pair' whose legs are אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.40.1) and אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.40.9). Re-collated: the token is byte tier at its own verse oshb:Isa.40.8, and the pair legs re-collate against each other at byte tier in both directions (as the row says); but the token itself returns tier NONE against oshb:Isa.40.1 and tier NONE against oshb:Isa.40.9, a 1cp-suffixed form against a 2mp-suffixed one. The campaign tier-disclosure standard requires every recurrence claim tier-labelled at write time; naming a token a 'member' of a 'byte-tier' pair without its own tier invites a byte-recurrence reading the bytes refuse. The book-order neighbour row does tier-label the same token (skeleton tier against oshb:Isa.40.3), so the asymmetry is internal to this batch.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair, device_notes only: state the token's own tier against the pair legs (tier NONE against oshb:Isa.40.1 and oshb:Isa.40.9) or drop the 'member of a byte-tier pair' framing and describe it as standing between the pair legs. No span, seam or evidence-ref change.

findings.claim: The close seam is warranted by a construction contrast between two forms of the same interrogative, named by the row as the signal that carries it, while the tier-1 addressee shift standing in the next verse's own bytes is neither named nor entered in observed_substrate_signals.
findings.grounds: device_notes states that the interrogative alone cannot distinguish this unit and that 'the signal that does is the shift in construction' from the bare measuring-question to the prepositional comparison-question at web:Isa.40.18. A construction contrast inside one particle is not one of the ruled tier-1 frame classes (superscription, massa header, hoy onset, divine-speech frame, addressee/scene shift, vocative, imperative onset). Re-derived from the bytes, a ruled signal is present and unused: the whole span is third person and unaddressed -- מִֽי מָדַ֨ד (oshb:Isa.40.12, tier: byte), מִֽי תִכֵּ֥ן (oshb:Isa.40.13, tier: byte), אֶת מִ֤י נוֹעָץ֙ (oshb:Isa.40.14, tier: byte), closing at נֶחְשְׁבוּ לֽוֹ (oshb:Isa.40.17, tier: byte) -- while the next verse opens a second-person-plural address, תְּדַמְּי֣וּן and תַּ֥עַרְכוּ (oshb:Isa.40.18, tier: byte, each against its own verse). No tier-3 corroboration sits at this seam either: the parashah layer marks oshb:Isa.40.16 and oshb:Isa.40.24, both cited by the row itself, and leaves oshb:Isa.40.17 unmarked (absence is not counterevidence, but it leaves the construction contrast alone on the seam).
findings.proposed_change: Field repair, no respan: name the second-person-plural addressee onset at oshb:Isa.40.18 as the tier-1 ground for the close, keeping the construction contrast as supporting texture, and add oracle_frame.addressee_shift to observed_substrate_signals. Span Isa.40.12-Isa.40.17 unchanged.

findings.claim: Two verbatim WEB verse runs are reproduced with no curly quotes at all, so the mandatory curly-quote-plus-inline-web-ref pairing is absent and the staged verbatim checker never evaluates them.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale reproduces the folded WEB text of web:Isa.40.12 (the measuring-questions verse) and of web:Isa.40.17 (the nations-as-nothing verse) as exact substrings of the staged WEB verse text, each introduced by an inline web: ref and each followed by ', pointed', but neither run carries an opening or closing curly quote anywhere. Run over the eight shipped rows, the staged WEB-quote checker reported quotes_checked 11 with zero flags: these two runs are not among the 11, so the Tier-0 verbatim arm passed over them untested. Curly quotes plus an inline web: ref in the same field are mandatory at every layer, and the same writer wraps correctly elsewhere in this batch (web:Isa.40.9, web:Isa.41.17, web:Isa.41.21, web:Isa.41.29).
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: wrap both WEB runs in curly double quotes in boundary_rationale so the verbatim arm can bind them to their inline web: refs. No content, span or evidence-ref change.

findings.claim: A cross-seam device is dismissed as a rendering-level echo and declared not a recurrence in the Hebrew at any tier; re-collated, the shared interrogative particle recurs at accent_stripped tier in both directions, and the fourfold pattern the row calls a rendering fact is fourfold in the Hebrew bytes.
findings.grounds: device_notes: 'The fourfold rebuke pattern at web:Isa.40.21 recurs in reduced form at web:Isa.40.28 in the following span; the resemblance is a rendering-level echo, not a recurrence in the Hebrew at any tier.' Re-collated from the staged bytes: הֲל֤וֹא (oshb:Isa.40.21, tier: byte at its own verse) re-collates against oshb:Isa.40.28 at accent_stripped tier, and reciprocally הֲל֨וֹא (oshb:Isa.40.28, tier: byte at its own verse) re-collates against oshb:Isa.40.21 at accent_stripped tier. The fourfold pattern is itself in the Hebrew, not in the rendering: the particle stands four times in the onset verse's own bytes -- הֲל֤וֹא, הֲל֣וֹא, הֲל֛וֹא, הֲלוֹא֙ (oshb:Isa.40.21, tier: byte, each against its own verse) -- so the object is Hebrew-side, not tier-4. The negative claim also names no count object: the clause-level comparison is genuinely tier NONE (the neighbour row states it that way, clause against clause), but the particle-level comparison is not, and the unqualified 'at any tier' is the form the bytes refuse. The device straddles this row's own close seam, so the tier misstatement lands on a cross-seam cohesion disclosure.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair, device_notes only: name the count object and restate at the collated tiers -- the clause-level comparison returns tier NONE while the shared interrogative particle re-collates at accent_stripped tier across the seam -- and drop 'rendering-level echo' for a Hebrew-side description. No span or seam change.

findings.claim: The onset seam is argued from a comparison-question construction expressly in place of an addressee shift and licensed by the operative-category allowance, which governs unit_type value selection rather than the choice of boundary driver; the disclaimed addressee shift does stand in the onset verse's own bytes.
findings.grounds: device_notes: 'This unit's boundaries are argued from the shared comparison-question construction opening web:Isa.40.18 and closing web:Isa.40.25 rather than from an imperative or addressee shift; disclosed here per the operative-category allowance since no woe, massa, or divine-speech-frame formula opens or closes this span.' The owner-ruled operative-category law is a unit_type provision -- each vocabulary line names the operative category rather than an exclusive grant, any closed-vocabulary value applying wherever the row's own bytes carry that form, with a one-sentence deviation disclosure -- so it does not license a boundary driver, and the sentence's stated ground (which boundary formulas are absent) is not the object the allowance governs. Re-derived from the bytes, the disclaimed signal is present at the onset: the preceding material is unaddressed third person through נֶחְשְׁבוּ לֽוֹ (oshb:Isa.40.17, tier: byte), and the onset verse opens a second-person-plural address, תְּדַמְּי֣וּן and תַּ֥עַרְכוּ (oshb:Isa.40.18, tier: byte, each against its own verse). The envelope the row does argue is byte-checked and honest at its stated tier (the shared prefix re-collates at accent_stripped tier, the fuller clauses tier NONE in both directions), so the finding is the warrant's grounding and its appeal to that allowance, not the envelope itself.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair, no respan: ground the onset on the second-person-plural addressee onset at oshb:Isa.40.18, keep the envelope as the close-side bracket, drop the operative-category appeal from the boundary argument (reserving it for a unit_type deviation if one is claimed), and add oracle_frame.addressee_shift to observed_substrate_signals. Span Isa.40.18-Isa.40.25 unchanged.

findings.claim: The onset verse's WEB text is reproduced verbatim with no curly quotes, leaving the mandatory pairing absent and the run untested by the staged verbatim arm.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale reads 'This unit's opening verse, web:Isa.40.18, reads To whom then will you liken God? Or what likeness will you compare to him?, pointed ...' -- the English run is an exact substring of the staged folded WEB text of that verse and carries no curly quote at either end. The staged WEB-quote checker over the eight shipped rows reported quotes_checked 11, zero flags; this run is not one of the 11. Curly quotes plus an inline web: ref in the same field are mandatory at every layer.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: wrap the web:Isa.40.18 run in curly double quotes in boundary_rationale. No content, span or evidence-ref change.

findings.claim: The close is carried in the prose by a single-witness parashah PE mark alone; no tier-1 signal is named at that seam, the next unit's onset verse appears in neither prose nor evidence refs, and the divine title this row itself sweeps recurs across the same seam without a cross-seam cohesion disclosure.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale gives the close as 'the unit's own end, at oshb:Isa.41.16, is then sealed by a PE parashah mark (single-witness), backing the division there' -- the only ground named at the seam. The mark is real (the staged inventory carries PE at MT 41:16 and the mark checker returns zero flags over these rows), but the parashah layer in the Prophets is tier-3 weak corroboration and never a boundary driver, so a close whose sole named ground is that mark leaves the seam without a driver. oshb:Isa.41.17 appears nowhere in the row: not in boundary_rationale, not in strongest_rejected_alternative, not in boundary_evidence_refs. The tier-1 ground that is available is unnamed: this span is second-person throughout -- וְאַתָּה֙ ... בְּחַרְתִּ֑יךָ (oshb:Isa.41.8, tier: byte), אַל תִּירָא֙ (oshb:Isa.41.10, tier: byte), וְאַתָּה֙ תָּגִ֣יל (oshb:Isa.41.16, tier: byte) -- while the four verses that follow the seam carry no second-person form at all, so the addressee is dropped exactly at the close. Cutting the other way, the title this row sweeps straddles that same seam: קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Isa.41.14, tier: byte) re-collates against oshb:Isa.41.16 and against oshb:Isa.41.20 at skeleton tier, two sites inside the span and one outside it; the row lists the three sites and their tiers but never says the cross-seam recurrence leaves its close undisturbed, the disclosure both neighbouring rows in this batch do carry for their own seams.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair, no respan: name the drop of the second-person addressee at oshb:Isa.41.17 as the tier-1 ground for the close with the PE mark demoted to corroboration, add oshb:Isa.41.17 to boundary_evidence_refs, and add the one-sentence cross-seam cohesion disclosure for the skeleton-tier title recurrence into oshb:Isa.41.20. Span Isa.41.8-Isa.41.16 unchanged.

findings.claim: The only high-band confidence in the batch, with the frontier flag not raised, is not survived by a close warrant whose sole named ground is single-witness tier-3 corroboration.
findings.grounds: confidence is 'high' and frontier_flag_considered is false, against a close at oshb:Isa.41.16 named only by the tier-3 PE mark (see the finding above) and an undisclosed skeleton-tier title recurrence across that seam. The onset is strong and tier-1 -- the adversative direct address וְאַתָּה֙ (oshb:Isa.41.8, tier: byte) naming Israel and Jacob as servant -- and the fear-not chain digit is exact (the second-person fear-not verb stands at 4 verses in chs 40-41, oshb:Isa.40.9, 41.10, 41.13, 41.14, re-swept independently), so the band is carried by one edge and not the other; every other row in this batch that rests an edge on marks plus content sits at medium or below.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: either lower confidence to medium, or raise the close warrant to a named tier-1 ground first and keep the band. No span change.

findings.claim: The closing verse's WEB text is reproduced verbatim with no curly quotes, leaving the run untested by the staged verbatim arm.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale reads 'closes at web:Isa.41.16, You will winnow them, and the wind will carry them away, and the whirlwind will scatter them. You will rejoice in Yahweh. You will glory in the Holy One of Israel..' -- an exact substring of the staged folded WEB text of that verse, with no curly quote at either end and a doubled sentence-final period where the wrapper would have closed. The staged WEB-quote checker over the eight shipped rows reported quotes_checked 11, zero flags; this run is not one of the 11.

findings.claim: The onset warrant calls the poor and needy this unit's addressee and twice asserts the seam falls without renaming the addressee; in the bytes they are third-person referents, the span carries no second-person form at all, and the seam is exactly where the preceding unit's second-person addressee is dropped.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale: 'addressed to the same unnamed \'poor and needy\' without renaming the addressee', repeated in strongest_rejected_alternative as 'without renaming the addressee'. Re-derived from the onset verse's own bytes, every reference to that pair is third person: הָעֲנִיִּ֨ים וְהָאֶבְיוֹנִ֜ים מְבַקְשִׁ֥ים ... לְשׁוֹנָ֖ם ... אֶעֱנֵ֔ם ... אֶעֶזְבֵֽם (oshb:Isa.41.17, tier: byte, each against its own verse) -- third-person plural subjects and third-person plural object suffixes, matched by the second witness rendering ('their tongue', 'answer them', 'forsake them'). Swept across the whole span, oshb:Isa.41.17-41.20 carries no second-person form, while the preceding unit is second-person throughout (וְאַתָּה֙ ... בְּחַרְתִּ֑יךָ at oshb:Isa.41.8 and וְאַתָּה֙ תָּגִ֣יל at oshb:Isa.41.16, tier: byte each). So the addressee is not carried across unchanged: it is dropped at this seam, which is the ruled tier-1 addressee/scene shift the row denies is in play. What is left holding the seam in the row as written is a topic characterisation plus the single-witness tier-3 PE mark at oshb:Isa.41.16, and observed_substrate_signals carries no addressee-shift key.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair, no respan: replace the 'addressed to ... without renaming the addressee' construction with the byte-true description (a third-person referent, and the second-person addressee of the preceding unit dropped at this seam), promote that drop to the named tier-1 ground with the PE mark as corroboration, and add oracle_frame.addressee_shift to observed_substrate_signals. Span Isa.41.17-Isa.41.20 unchanged.

The staged WEB-quote checker over the eight shipped rows reported quotes_checked 11, zero flags; this run is not one of the 11, while the same row's web:Isa.41.17 run is wrapped correctly and was checked.

findings.claim: The opening bound is warranted by a content characterisation plus a single-witness tier-3 PE mark, with no tier-1 frame signal named in the onset verse's own bytes, although the closed-vocabulary value carried by this row applies only where the unit's bounds are argued from tier-1 seams.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale gives the onset as 'a third-person divine presentation of an unnamed servant figure, opening a fresh unit distinct from the trial-speech material closing chapter 41. A parashah PE mark (single-witness) sits at oshb:Isa.41.29, immediately before this unit's own onset.' Neither element is a ruled tier-1 frame signal: the first is a content characterisation and the second is Prophets parashah, tier-3 weak corroboration that is never a driver. The close, by contrast, is tier-1 sound and the row names it -- כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הָאֵ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.42.5, tier: byte), a divine-owned frame, with the koh-amar digit re-swept and exact (4 verses in chs 41-43, all divine-owned, none in ch 41). Re-derived from the bytes, a tier-1 ground is available at the onset and unused: the preceding trial speech addresses the idols in the second person plural -- הֵן אַתֶּ֣ם מֵאַ֔יִן (oshb:Isa.41.24, tier: byte) and אִמְרֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.41.26, tier: byte) -- and that addressee is dropped at הֵ֤ן עַבְדִּי֙ (oshb:Isa.42.1, tier: byte), which the row's device_notes touches only as cross-seam particle texture. observed_substrate_signals carries no addressee- or scene-shift key.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair, no respan: name the drop of the trial speech's second-person-plural addressee at oshb:Isa.42.1 as the tier-1 ground for the opening bound, with the PE mark at oshb:Isa.41.29 kept as corroboration, and add the corresponding addressee/scene-shift key to observed_substrate_signals. Span Isa.42.1-Isa.42.4 unchanged.

findings.claim: observed_substrate_signals carries an inclusio-bracket key the row's prose never argues, and omits any speech-formula key for the divine-speech frame the row itself names as what carries its own bound.
findings.grounds: observed_substrate_signals is servant_song.unnamed_referent and oracle_frame.inclusio_bracket. The row's prose argues no inclusio: it argues a sustained justice-noun thread through 3 of the span's 4 verses (re-swept and exact: the mishpat noun stands at 3 verses in ch 42, oshb:Isa.42.1, 42.3, 42.4) and two devices crossing the seams. Meanwhile boundary_rationale states that the fresh divine-speech-frame onset at oshb:Isa.42.5 'is what carries this unit's own bound', and כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הָאֵ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.42.5, tier: byte) is a divine-speech frame -- a signal class with a key in the sanctioned dotted taxonomy that the field does not record. The field is a dependent field of the row's drivers, so the row's own stated close driver should appear in it.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: add a speech_formula key for the divine-speech-frame onset at oshb:Isa.42.5 to observed_substrate_signals, and either argue the bracket in device_notes or drop oracle_frame.inclusio_bracket. No span or evidence-ref change.
